Bill.BriefDescription: Creating an oversight committee to review alternative public works contracting procedures.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to an oversight committee to review alternativepublic works contracting procedures; and adding a new section tochapter 39.10 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 39.10 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) There is established within the office of financial managementan oversight committee to review the utilization of the alternativepublic works contracting procedures authorized under this chapter,specifically to further good contracting practices on generalcontractor/construction manager (GC/CM) projects for the benefit of thetaxpayers. The membership of the committee shall includerepresentatives from the appropriate segments of the contracting,subcontracting, and design industries, as well as appropriate labororganizations, and public bodies authorized to use the alternativepublic works contracting procedures under this chapter. The directorshall maintain a balance between representatives from public agenciesand the private sector when appointing members to the committee, and p. 1 SB 6670shall consider the recommendations of established organizationsrepresenting the contracting, subcontracting, design industries, andorganized labor in making the appointments. (2) The committee shall meet quarterly beginning after July 1,2004. The director or his or her designee shall chair the committeeand the office of financial management shall provide staff support forthe committee. (3) Public bodies utilizing the alternative contracting proceduresauthorized under this chapter shall provide any requested informationconcerning implementation of projects under this chapter to thecommittee in a timely manner, excepting any trade secrets orproprietary information. (4) The committee shall report to the governor by December 10,2004, and every year thereafter, concerning its findings andrecommendations.
